FX.Sniffer wrote: Cable; there is nothing interestig on LTF so by looking at daily we see a bullish move created a LQ gap preceeded by a failed inverted pinbar which is a sign of trapped sellers and an area where price tends to bounce from. On the upper side there is compression (multiple FTRs) and a flag limit where price might create a fakeout.

H4 and what to expect on it; price could drop from the current range to the trapped sellers area where we can buy targeting the higher levels, or price could rise to the fakeout area where we can sell targeting the lower level. Any significant price action other than what has been planned here could change the whole plan.

The upper side of story has happened twice giving a second chance for entry, and now it's the lower side turn.

author: sunnytrader1984
text:
FXSniffer, May I?

Romant, Bullish engulfing candle happening at a right place (in demand) would make a lot of sense, at the wrong place (in supply) would also make a lot of sense (non). Now depends which sense you choose.

Here is for you, take the place where you marked you went long and just look 1 cm above, do you see a strong DAILY supply? For most of the traders here on RTM, this would have said already, DONT BUY, DONT BUY, DONT BUY!

But you bought, now why did you buy.....because they made you buy. A strong bullish looking candle right into the supply serves well to catch retail longs for them to put their shorts in. This is a simple sentence, the day it makes sense for you.....you will be on your way.

Here is one small suggestion, I wont call advice, coz I am not good enough. Forget about engulfing candles....why? because an engulfing candle on H4 might just be a lot of compression on M15. Here is what you need to start looking for....ZONE ENGULFS, DP ENGULFS, POINTY PLACE ENGULFS...dont get scared now, these are all the same things, we call them differently.

I can suggest you where to start....CAPTAIN P's trading journal. read his first post...take his charts and go through each of them thinking for yourself, why he did what he did.

There are goldmines here on many journals, you need to find your niche. Everybody has a different trading style, make your own!

Good luck on this beautiful journey!

author: Infest
text:
Very important lesson for lots of traders, even the expierenced one's.

Gold is in a HTF down trend so what we want is to enter shorts as long as price prints lower lows. And this fact occured just a few days ago on April 4th. Accomplished by big momentum down candles, so in no way we want to look for possible longs here, maybe scalp one's but in no case any long setups. We let the big boys decide to print higher highs on HTF so that we can enter at the retest with the lowest risk, but trying to get the turning point just doesn't make lots of sense.

I'm also in this progress which gave me lots of "Aha-moments" and some very easy entries with ZERO risk and ZERO drawdown - because you go with the trend. So all you have to do is find where the big decisions were made from the big boys.

FX Sniffers last post contains all the information. Especially his first picture. "Engulfed previous low - engulfed previous low - engulfed previous low"... this should always be the first thing that comes in mind when looking for trading decisions. And on daily the level at 1589 (support line) that got engulfed by big momentum candles AND engulfing previous low makes up a more than perfect entry. I do not know how many traders took this trade at the 1589-level, but I am quite sure that many many of them just earned their money not even for this month, but also for the next - if they held it like FX Sniffer did.
